The ends do justify the means. And yes, people who can't or won't adopt digital distribution are impacting those who do, because producing, shipping, and cutting in retailers on a piece of the pie represents additional cost, and it's a cost that is spread out across all distribution methods. 2-3 years ago a AAA game would run you $50, $60 for select franchise releases. Now we're seeing costs in the $70-80 range for standard edition new releases. Part of that increase is covering the increased cost of physical distribution. It's a fundamental law of manufacturing and distribution. The more you order, the cheaper it gets by the unit. Developers aren't ordering the same number of physical copies for release any more so the cost per unit goes up. But do you see that difference at the retailer? Nope. Same price as digital. So who is paying for the difference? Everyone.

Physical distribution is old-school and it's going away. Everyone resisted the transition from beta to VHS, cassette to CD, CRT to LCD, analog cable to digital. The list of technologies rendered obsolete by newer technologies is lengthy and significant. For you to think for even a fraction of a second that you can avoid that trend is a bit naive. It would be a benefit to you if you would stop blaming developers for your shitty ISP. Game developers have nothing to do with the download caps imposed by your ISP. Your fight is with the people imposing the limits. If you had 200-300GB/month to play with for the same price you pay now, you likely would be singing an entirely different tune. And when all that's preventing you from embracing the inevitable is handled by your ISP, trying to find fault with game developers for not catering to your minority circumstances is not very nice.

There is nothing you can do to stop the transition to digital distribution. You're wasting your time trying.
